entry.name: Alley Scavengers
entry.intro: Ash-crawlers scrabble out of the rubble.

nodes.text: The candle-maker keeps one eye on the window. "Tallow's dear. Warded tallow is dearer. I sell the plain kind and tell nobody it's plain." The wicks hang in rows like pale ribs.
"The Watch buy by the dozen, never by the pound. Ask yourself why."
A lodging-keeper counts coins into a tin without looking at them. "Beds by the night, none by the week. Nobody who sleeps here is here in the morning."
"Quiet house. Keep it quiet."
A bent figure sweeps ash from a drain-run shrine. "They leave the old ones here when the cremation salt runs out. I say the names. Somebody should."
"Don't thank me. Thank the salt, when there is any."
The pawnbroker weighs a tin spoon on a brass scale. "Spoons, shoes, a good tooth. Nothing from the cages; that's the Proctor's trade, not mine."
"Nobody pawns a name. They'd get more for it."
Chalk marks cover the walls of the abandoned den, some scratched out. A squatter hunches among them. "Runners used this room. Then the Proctor's sweeps came. Don't read the numbers aloud."
"The ones still chalked are the ones still alive. Maybe."
Soot drifts through the choked shrine. The keeper wipes a small stone saint with her sleeve. "Ash doesn't fall here, it settles. It settles on everything. Even on prayer."
"A candle costs more than the prayer. Say it anyway."
A hauler hangs his gloves by the stove, grey to the wrist. "Cart's due by third bell. Bone dust gets in the lungs. Don't breathe deep on the track."
"Twelve years on the cart. My knees went before my mind. Lucky."
The bone chandler rolls pale wax in his palms. "Mortar's cheap, candles are cheaper. Burn them near a Spent and they sleep sound. That's what the Guild likes."
"Everything on this shelf was somebody. Don't ask who."
Rows of unlit stubs line the shrine for the uncremated Spent. A sweeper pauses. "The salt ration is short again this month. We keep them company until it isn't."
"They harden slow, the old ones. We sit with them."
The chandler skims a pot of grey tallow. "Guild-warded, stamped, taxed. Mine's unwarded, so I sell it quiet and cheap. Don't tell the vats."
"Warded tallow burns clean. It also costs a body. That's the arithmetic."
A dredger lies on a bunk with his boots on. "Sixteen hours on the catwalk. The vats hum all night; you stop hearing it, then you hear nothing else."
"Orlov pays on the third bell. Mostly."
A cracked saint stands in an alcove at the end of the alley. A woman lights a dip-candle in front of it. "For the ones who went into the vats. Guild says they were rendered with honour."
"Honour weighs less than salt."
A man sits cross-legged in the cliff shrine, wrists still marked by cuffs. "Last prayers before the Crucible. It's a small shrine for a long queue."
"They'll come for me at third bell. Or the next. Sit a while."
A clerk copies a Watch log with a shaking hand. "Names in, names out. Some of the names don't come out. I just write the ledger."
"Don't read the cell sheet. It's not for readers."

entry.name: Sunk Ward: the Drowned Runoff Grate
The Sluice Undercroft
entry.description: Node 00, the hub: a flooded undercroft with six bunks, a brazier, the Tinker's Hearth, the Apothecary's Slab and the Water-Lock Basin, below the Sunk Ward.

entry.name: Drowned Runoff Grate
entry.description: Node 01: the egress and checkpoint where the drains meet the streets. Flood-lock tablets stand under the silt.

markers.label: A forgotten flood-lock tablet
markers.note: Vesper wipes the silt off a bronze lock-plate and reads the old sluice routes aloud. The drains answer.

entry.name: Corvo's Gate
entry.description: Node 1d: the Third Ward gate, where Bailiff Corvo keeps a bribable post.

markers.label: World map: the Third Ward road

entry.name: The Slag Gate
entry.description: Node 07: the gate out of the Sunk Ward, beneath the Crucible Watchpost. Beyond it lies Upper Cinderreach.

markers.label: The raised portcullis
markers.note: The winch has lifted it. Beyond the chain-teeth, a road climbs toward Upper Cinderreach.

entry.name: Alleyway Junction 7
entry.description: Node 02: a street crossing in the Seventh Ward where Captain Vane has sealed the grates.

markers.label: The old Watch armory cache
markers.note: Behind a loose course of bricks: Kaelen's old Watch cache, a soot-black bellows and a heavy plate for Berek to rework.

entry.name: Ash-Crawl Crossroads
entry.description: Node 03: an open-air culling station where the slum alleys meet, with the Seventh Ward Toll-Pen beside the cages.

markers.label: The Seventh Ward Toll-Pen
markers.note: A boy with a chalked number on his shirt counts sentries on his fingers. The lock gives. He keeps counting until the grate is behind you.

markers.label: The cage-seal rubbings
markers.note: Maren spreads grey linen over the open cage seals and rubs. The Clerisy's cipher rises in white lines. St. Lyra's name is in it.

entry.name: The Fourth Kiln
entry.description: Node 04: the bone-mill that mortars the Inquisition's watch-posts out of uncremated Spent.

markers.label: A pile of black-iron wedges
markers.note: Dunstan lifts the splitting wedges from the ruined mill one at a time, like a man picking his own name out of a ledger.

entry.name: The Tallow Vats
entry.description: Node 05: the Guild's rendering vats and still-rooms, where Tallow Dredgers boil the district's dead.

markers.label: Elyse's counter-still
markers.note: A coil of copper pipe and a leaking alum drum in the corner of a tenement block. Elyse tips a measure of clean tallow into a flask and corks it with her thumb.

entry.name: Crucible Watchpost
entry.description: Node 06: the fortified post above the Slag Gate, with the winch that lifts it.

markers.label: The Crag-Sight Overlook
markers.note: Hollis climbs the chimney stack and drops the outer counterweight from the gutter. The gate's reinforcements will have to take the long way round.
